newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian chancellor to resign on Saturday - source.
newsitem.headline: Austrian chancellor to resign on Saturday - source.

text.p: Austrian Chancellor Franz Vranitzky is likely to resign on Saturday, a senior source in his Social Democratic Party said on Saturday.
Speaking on condition of anonymity, the sources told Reuters that reports of Vranitzky's impending resignation in two Austrian dailies on Saturday were "not far from the truth".
"I would assume that this will happen," the source said.
Vranitzky, 59, had called a meeting of the party's executive committee for 4 p.m. (1500 GMT) to offer his resignation, the source said.
Two leading Austrian dailies, Der Standard and Kurier, said Vranitzky was likely to be succeeded as chancellor and head of the Social Democrats by Finance Minister Viktor Klima, 49.
Vranitzky's spokesman Karl Krammer declined to comment on the reports. "There is no comment whatsoever from our side. I haven't even spoken to the chancellor myself," he said.
Vranitzky, a former banker and one-time professional basketball player who became chancellor in 1986, has repeatedly been reported to have become tired of politics.
The popular daily Kurier said Klima would be replaced by fellow Social Democrat Rudolf Scholten, Minister for Transport and Telecommunications.

The Social Democrats and the conservatives last weekend struck a deal on the sale of the state's controlling stake in flagship bank Creditanstalt to arch-rival Bank Austria, after a bitter dispute that had threatened to split the coalition.
The coalition was formed after a snap election in December 1995 after the conservatives quit the previous government following a heated row over how to cut Austria's growing budget deficit.
